Find the $x$-intercept of the line $y = 6 - 3x$ by setting $y = 0 \implies x = 2$.

walkthrough:
Find the $x$-coordinate of the intersection point $P$ where $y = 3$:
$$6 - 3x = 3 \implies 3x = 3 \implies x = 1$$

Find the $x$-intercept of the straight line $y = 6 - 3x$ by setting $y = 0$:
$$6 - 3x = 0 \implies 3x = 6 \implies x = 2$$

Calculate the area under the curve from $x = 0$ to $x = 1$ using definite integration:
$$\int_0^1 9(5x+4)^{-1/2} dx = \left[ \frac{9(5x+4)^{1/2}}{\frac{1}{2} \times 5} \right]_0^1 = \left[ \frac{18}{5}\sqrt{5x+4} \right]_0^1 = \frac{18}{5}(3) - \frac{18}{5}(2) = \frac{18}{5} = 3.6$$

Calculate the area of the triangle under the line from $x = 1$ to $x = 2$:
$$\text{Area}(\text{Triangle}) = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2}(2 - 1)(3) = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5$$

Sum the two areas to find the total shaded area:
$$\text{Total Area} = \frac{18}{5} + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{36 + 15}{10} = \frac{51}{10} = 5.1$$
